chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from al-Walid ibn Sabih from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Any woman who applies perfume, then goes out from her house, is cursed until she returns to her house, whenever she returns.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman wearing perfume when she goes out?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.s.) declares that a woman who applies perfume and exits her home is cursed until she returns, emphasizing the etiquette of modesty and the specific context of wearing perfume for others rather than one's husband. This ruling highlights the importance of a woman's conduct in public spaces and the potential for her fragrance to attract unwanted attention, which is seen as a form of modesty violation. The hadith underscores the significance of maintaining a balance between personal adornment and public decorum in Islamic tradition.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam  Ja’far  Sadiq  (a.s.)  narrates  that  the  Holy  Prophet (s.a.w.s.) said, “If a woman goes out after applying perfume, she will be cursed till the time she returns.”
